clue.text: Strike by those who provoke tough questions  …

blocks.note: to brain someone is to strike them on the head
people who provoke or needle others; 'by' places this piece beside the first

explanation.surface: A walkout by agitators who keep asking awkward questions, running on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 8 across for the surface only; each clue is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles that make you think hard are a common name for difficult problems or riddles.

clue.text: First farm building that includes everything

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building
one is first, as in number one; it follows the farm building

explanation.surface: The first outbuilding on a farm, which holds everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'number one barn', with the number placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means with no exceptions at all, so a statement qualified this way covers every case.

clue.text: Reform made in first-class community of scholars

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a different shape, so the letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the other piece

blocks.note: ace means excellent, first-class
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An educational reform introduced within an elite academic community.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the world of universities and academics, i.e. the scholarly community collectively.

clue.text: Muse tends to get moving, when absolutely unavoidable

indicators.note: getting moving means shifting about, so these letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A goddess of inspiration bestirs herself only when she has no choice.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'needs must when the devil drives', said when circumstances force your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is used when necessity compels an action, so it applies when there is no alternative.

clue.text: Relieved after cold is finished

indicators.note: the solution is what comes after the cold abbreviation, so that opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps
ceased means stopped or finished

explanation.surface: Feeling better once a cold has run its course.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the answer, placed after C, is 'finished': C plus EASED makes CEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain or tension that has been lessened is said to have been alleviated or relieved.

clue.text: Pull into sensible space for parking items in transit

definitions.text: space for parking items in transit

indicators.note: into means one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: sage means wise or sensible
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Pulling into a sensible parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parking' suggests cars, but here it means putting cargo away during a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships and planes this is the room where luggage and cargo are packed away for the journey.

clue.text: Adjust position of concrete sign having small omission

indicators.note: an omission leaves something out, and here what goes is the abbreviation for small

blocks.note: concrete in the sense of actual, tangible
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, removed from the previous word

explanation.surface: Repositioning a concrete road sign with a small piece missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the material of a sign but means real.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something back into line means to move it to a corrected position, i.e. adjust where it sits.

clue.text: Couple indicate boundary for averge children in the traditional family?

definitions.text: averge children in the traditional family

blocks.note: a couple is two
to point is to indicate
in cricket a boundary is a hit that scores four runs

explanation.surface: A couple point out the boundary line, musing on typical family size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Averge' is a typo in the source for average. The figure is the much-quoted average number of children in a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The statistic was long cited as how many kids a typical household had, becoming shorthand for conventional family life.

clue.text: …  fighting to report atmosphere in docklands?

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the words that follow are to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a wharf is a quay in docklands, and air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: Continuing from 1 across, the strike turns into a battle at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition-by-example of docklands air.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations or groups is the general term covering combat and battles.

clue.text: Organic food processor

blocks.note: surface reading: a kitchen appliance for making organic meals
setter's reading: a body organ that breaks down what you eat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Organic' suggests chemical-free produce, but here it means being a bodily organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The digestive organ churns and breaks down meals, so it literally processes what we eat inside the body.

clue.text: Lie flat before running for a quick start

definitions.text: before running for a quick start
definitions.note: the phrase that precedes 'running' in the idiom for starting quickly

blocks.note: first meaning: throw yourself down on the floor

blocks.clueFragment: before running for a quick start
blocks.note: second meaning: the opening of an idiom completed by the word running

explanation.surface: Advice to drop flat before setting off at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: To hit the ground running is to start a new job or project at full speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means dropping prone on the floor, and with 'running' added it means beginning energetically from the outset.

clue.text: Way of doing complex scores on page

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so these letters are mixed up
on means placed after, so the piece before this word goes second and the one after it goes first

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing an intricate method of writing musical scores on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex scores' reads like elaborate music, but complex is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A method or series of steps taken to achieve a result is a standard synonym.

clue.text: One records attack being repulsed first

indicators.note: an attack that is repulsed is driven back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a raid is a sudden attack
1ST, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone documenting how an assault was beaten back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One records' means 'one who records', a person keeping a daily log.
explanation.definitionFit: Somebody who keeps a daily journal is writing down events, so they are a person who records.

clue.text: Woman capturing the hearts of both Miro and Genet

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters of each name are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters of the painter's name
the three central letters of the writer's name

explanation.surface: A woman who wins over both the Spanish artist Miró and the French writer Genet.
explanation.walkthrough: Miró and Genet are famous enough for the surface to sound like an art-world romance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, and crosswords commonly define any given name by its holder's sex.

clue.text: Put the men into another formation — the last of many?

indicators.note: putting troops into a new formation rearranges them, so the letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant reorganising soldiers yet again, sighing that it is the latest of countless times.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means occurring after a great many previous ones, i.e. the latest in a very long series.

clue.text: A poem Dante hasn't finished about outrageous stage character

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the last letter of the name is dropped
about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the poet's name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Dante leaves a poem unfinished about some scandalous theatrical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime the dame is a comic older woman traditionally played by a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: This loud cross-dressed comic figure from Christmas theatre is famously over the top, hence outrageous.

clue.text: Checked out clothing and got fresh

blocks.note: first meaning: put a garment on to see if it fits
second meaning: took liberties, attempted something cheeky

explanation.surface: A shopper who tried on clothes and then became overfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'try it on' in British slang is to push your luck or attempt a cheeky deception.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes testing garments for fit and idiomatically means being impudent or making a pass.

clue.text: Split is happening as Romeo turns to whiskey

indicators.note: one letter turning into another means it is swapped out for the new one

blocks.note: in train means under way, happening
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
Whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A break-up is under way as Romeo takes to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' introduces the swap: the R in the phrase for happening is replaced by W.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase means divided into two parts, so it describes something that has been cut apart.

clue.text: Stupid to get told off over his mess

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of place, so these letters are jumbled
making a mess of something jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged too

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: It is foolish to get scolded about the mess he left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' looks like scolded, but off is an instruction on told alone. In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like a dimwit or blockhead means being foolish and slow-witted.

clue.text: Issue that's supertough, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A problem that is extremely hard, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a problem but means offspring; a sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for children or descendants, and this slang term means a small child.

clue.text: In haste, fan offered accommodation for Italian chap

indicators.note: in tells us the solution sits inside the following words
the words before this phrase give housing to the solution, holding it within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: A fan hurriedly gave lodging to a man from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Italian form of Stephen, a common man's first name in Italy.

clue.text: African managed to acquire magic rod

indicators.note: acquiring something means taking it in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
a wand is a magician's rod

explanation.surface: A man from Africa got hold of a magic stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a central African republic is, by nationality, a person from that continent.

clue.text: Issue from available supply

blocks.note: a new book or record that is out is on sale and available
a flow is a steady supply, as of oil or cash

explanation.surface: Something emerging from stock that is ready to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' here is the verb-turned-noun of pouring out, not a problem or offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue can be a discharge or emergence of liquid, which is a stream leaving a source.

clue.text: What all totally empty reservoirs principally lack

definitions.text: What all totally empty reservoirs principally lack

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so each word gives its leading letter

blocks.note: the leading letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a bone-dry reservoir is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reservoirs exist to store the liquid supply, so an empty one is missing exactly that.

clue.text: Plant that's yellow, say, with an orange head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry
e.g., for example
taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: Describing a yellow plant with an orange flower head.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic term for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an aromatic herb used in cooking, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: One who sees the truth about top celebrities

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
the A-list is the group of most famous stars

explanation.surface: Someone clear-eyed about how big stars really are.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatic person accepts situations as they actually are, facing facts without illusions.

clue.text: Drop a fellow outside bar

indicators.note: outside means the first part wraps around the second

blocks.note: taken as written
a don is a fellow of a university college
to bar is to prohibit

explanation.surface: Dropping off a man outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is the verb meaning prohibit; A and DON together wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a plan or person is to give up on or desert them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The owner soon redesigned a dull place to live

indicators.note: a redesign rebuilds something in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A property owner quickly remodels a boring place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a small, sleepy settlement with little going on, hence a boring spot to reside.
